L90: ## Types: string, not ClassLabel
L91: The columns and nested fields are plain **`string`**, **`int64`**, **`bool`** and
L92: **`double`**. There is no `ClassLabel` metadata for any enumerated column and the
L93: `dataset_info` block is deliberately absent from the dataset card, so the "values
L94: observed" lists below are documentation, not a schema constraint the file enforces.
L95: Later batches may add values to these sets; per the release contract in
L96: [`INCREMENTAL.md`](INCREMENTAL.md), values are only ever **added**, never renamed.
L97: The shards are written with pyarrow from an **explicit schema**, not inferred from
L98: their contents, and that schema carries a `huggingface` features block. Two
L99: consequences:
L100: - `load_dataset` restores the nested types — `List` of struct, `Image`, `Video` — so
L101:   a row comes back with decoded PIL images and Python lists of dicts. A plain
L102:   `pyarrow.parquet` or DuckDB reader sees the underlying arrow types given in the
L103:   tables below; an `Image` or `Video` is `struct<bytes: binary, path: string>`.
L104: - A column carries its real type however sparse it is: `bridge.cmds_counted`,
L105:   `bridge.gripper_cmds`, `bridge.failed_cmds` and `timing.duration_s` — sourced only
L106:   from `results.csv` — are never NULL on the table's 162 rows but NULL on 15 of the
L107:   27 reset rows, and are `int64` there too; the three `tokens` fields, filled from
L108:   the trace where `results.csv` has none, are NULL on 3 rows of the table (and 2
L109:   reset rows) and are still `int64`. The `trials/` and `reset/` shards share one
L110:   schema, b01's and b02's alike.

L112: media (5–7), 4 are structs of scalars (13–16), 1 is a struct with a list inside

L114: ## How missing data is represented — read this before writing a WHERE clause
L115: 
L116: The families disagree, and the difference is load-bearing. The same rules hold
L117: inside the nested structs.

L119: |---|---|---|

L128: The rule across every file in this release is: **a missing value is an absence,
L129: never a literal.** No column anywhere carries `NA`, `N/A`, `NULL`, `nan` or `-1`
L130: standing in for "no value". This is not cosmetic. A loader reading a CSV with
L131: pandas' default parsing turns both a blank cell and a literal `NA` into the same
L132: `None`, so a sentinel cannot express anything a blank does not — it can only produce
L133: two spellings of one state and force every consumer to handle both.
L134: **"Not applicable" is therefore carried by a positive column, not by a sentinel.**

L137: a blank timestamp field the reader has to interpret. When a later batch adds a

L164: ## Notes on individual columns
L165: **`bridge.cmds_counted` is not a command count.** It is the final value of the
L166: server's budget counter, which only increments for commands that consume budget.
L167: Free commands (`status`, `help`, `state`, `deproject`, and for knowledge-enabled
L168: sessions also `episode` and `experience`) do not increment it. A session whose
L169: bridge log holds 96 requests can carry `cmds_counted = 56`. The true per-command
L170: count is the number of `traces[].calls[]` elements on the same row; do not present
L171: `cmds_counted` as "number of robot commands".
L172: **`tokens.input` is cache-inclusive and is not a billing figure.** Cache hit rates
L173: in these runs are high, which is why the median is ~5.7 M tokens for sessions that
L174: issue on the order of a hundred commands. Cached and uncached input are not
L175: separated in b01, so no cost can be reconstructed from this field. `tokens.output`
L176: includes reasoning tokens, and `tokens.reasoning` is the reasoning-only subset of
L177: that same total — **do not add the two**.
L178: **The three `tokens` fields have two sources and one definition.** The run's
L179: `results.csv` carries them for most rows; where it does not, the builder
L180: (`fill_tokens_from_traces` in `build_trials_table.py`) sums the `usage` of every
L181: `turn.completed` event in the session's trace — `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`,
L182: `reasoning_output_tokens` — which
L183: is the same accounting the results file was written from: on every session
L184: (table and reset rows together) that has both, the two agree on every row, and the
L185: builder asserts that. b02's rows were filled the same way, so the definition is one
L186: across batches. The fields are present on **159 of the 162 rows** (and 25
L187: of the 27 reset rows) and NULL on 3 — the sessions that never completed a turn,
L188: because codex emits usage only when a turn completes: the 3 `timed_out` sessions.
L189: The 2 reset rows without them are the 1 `aborted` reset session and 1 reset session
L190: that ended without a turn completion (all five are listed under "Known schema
L191: issues", item 7). `verify_dataset.py` fails if a token count is NULL on any row that
L192: is neither timed out, aborted nor without a `timing.duration_s`. The token medians
L193: in the dataset card's Results table and in `DETAILS.md` §4 were computed **before**
L194: this fill, over the rows that had tokens in `results.csv` (their `n_tok` column), and
L195: were left as they are; the fields now cover more rows than those tables used.
L196: **`timing.duration_s` is session wall clock**, from `AGENT_START_S` to
L197: `AGENT_END_S`. It includes operator waiting and the agent's closing report, so it
L198: runs longer than the "report boundary" task time used in the paper by roughly
L199: 0.8 min. The maximum observed value, 5,411 s, is the 90-minute cap.
L200: **`timing.start_epoch_s` / `end_epoch_s` are integers, not timestamps.** No
L201: timezone-aware timestamp column is shipped. Convert explicitly, e.g.
L202: `to_timestamp(timing.start_epoch_s)` in DuckDB. Every row carries a start time; they
L203: span **2026-09-04 22:00:36Z to 2026-09-15 02:42:03Z**; session directory names span
L204: 2026-09-04 to 2026-09-14.
L205: **`arms` provenance is mixed.** 54 of the 189 released sessions (table and reset
L206: rows together) did not record `ARMS` in `session.env`; for those the value was
L207: inferred from the session directory name. The column does not record which rows were
L208: inferred, so any analysis that turns on the left/right/dual distinction should treat
L209: that subset as lower-confidence.
L210: **`reasoning_summary` is the model's words, not a generated abstract.** Nothing is
L211: paraphrased and nothing is truncated: it is the concatenation, in order, of the
L212: `text` of every `reasoning` and `message` step of `traces[]`, separated by a blank
L213: line. `error` steps are not in it. The builder would clip a summary at 200,000
L214: characters; on b01 the longest is 29,130, so no row is clipped. It is there so that
L215: a reader can grep what the agent was thinking without unnesting `traces[]`; to know
L216: *when* it thought it, read `traces[]`, where the same text sits on the step.
L217: **The run configuration is legible from `batch` and `interface_text`, not from a
L218: column.** Until 2026-09-15 the row carried `run_config_json`, a JSON object with
L219: `harness`, `harness_version`, `interface`, `knowledge_mode`, `knowledge_scope`,
L220: `service_tier` and `tools_inherited`. It is gone. The ablation those keys encoded is
L221: in the `batch` name — which contains `bare` or `full` for the tool surface, plus the
L222: model and effort of the cell — and the tool surface the agent actually saw is the
L223: `interface_text` on the row (11 distinct documents; the `bare` ones are the short
L224: ones). The knowledge-loop ablations are read the same way: their `batch` names carry
L225: `ckpt`, `kn`, `mx` or the read-only `ckptro` / `mxro`, and the card's `twopairs`
L226: comparison excludes them by that token. `prompt_file` is gone for the same reason: the prompt text is inline and every
L227: distinct text ships under `documents/`.

L304: ### How `traces[]` was built
L305: 
L306: This is a reconstruction from two different transcript formats, and the joins it
L307: makes are worth stating, because they are where a reader's trust should be spent.
L308: **codex sessions (180 of the 189).** One element per `item.completed` event, in file
L309: order; `item.started` carries nothing the completion does not. `reasoning`,
L310: `agent_message`, `file_change` and `error` items map to their `kind` directly;
L311: `command_execution` carries the command, its aggregated output and its exit code.
L312: **A robot-bridge call is not identifiable from the command string.** Measured on b01:
L313: of the 14,960
L314: codex commands that produced a bridge answer, **3,306 — 22% — never mention the
L315: client** (`robot_client.py`): the agents write their own wrappers (`scratch/step.py`,
L316: `pose_and_capture.py`, batch loops), and a wrapper's name says nothing. Conversely 52
L317: commands mention the client and produce no answer at all. So a call is identified
L318: **from the output**: every bridge answer is a top-level JSON object beginning
L319: `{"ok"`, carrying an integer `id` equal to the recorded request's `cmd_id`. An object
L320: that is *nested* inside a larger JSON is rejected — those are other sessions' logs
L321: the agent printed back with `cat` or `sed`, and their ids would collide because every
L322: session numbers its requests from 1 (73 such objects in 4 sessions). A step that
L323: **took a picture** is one whose answer carries an integer `capture`, and that value
L324: is the capture index.
L325: **The eleven dual-arm trials run two bridges**, each numbering its requests and its
L326: captures from 1, and **only the left bridge's records are published**. Each answer is
L327: therefore attributed to an arm by the first of these that decides:
L328: 1. the answer's own `arm` field, if it has one;
L329: 2. the *k*-th bridge segment of the command line issued the *k*-th answer (segments
L330:    split on newline, `&&`, `;`, `||`); a segment without `--arm` drives the left
L331:    bridge;
L332: 3. the capture's file path — `frames_right/` versus `frames/`;
L333: 4. a consistency test: an answer carrying a `capture` must join a row whose `cmd` is
L334:    `frames`, and an id that is unknown or already claimed belongs to the other bridge.
L335: A right-bridge call therefore has `arm = 'right'` with `cmd_id = null` and
L336: `cmd = ''`: the answer is real and its `ok` is recorded, but there is no record row
L337: to name it from. That is 1,503 of the table's 22,679 calls, all of them b01's — b02
L338: froze no dual-arm session.
L339: **claude sessions (9 of the 189).** A different shape: the harness emits one content
L340: block per assistant line and the tool result arrives in the next `user` line, and
L341: **the bridge's answer is usually not in the transcript at all** — only 521 of those
L342: sessions' 971 recorded requests left an answer in it. Both sides carry the same wall
L343: clock, so the recorded requests are swept onto the `Bash` steps in time order, each
L344: step taking the requests that fall before the next step's start; all 971 are
L345: attached this way. Two further properties of these nine rows: the `thinking` blocks
L346: are **838 of 922 empty** — they carry only an opaque signature, which is never
L347: published — so the model's readable text is thin (16,789 characters of thinking plus
L348: 16 message blocks over nine trials), and **378 tool results are images** (131 MB of
L349: base64), replaced by the placeholder `[image content omitted; the file is named in
L350: the command]`.
L351: **Coverage.** 20,760 of the 21,112 recorded requests in the `evaluated` split are
L352: attached to the step that issued them (**98.3%**); all 2,545 in the reset split are
L353: (**23,305 of 23,657, 98.5%**, over the release). The **352 unattached** ones are
L354: requests whose answer never reached the transcript — they are listed per session in
L355: `build_stats-b01.json` and `build_stats-b02.json`, and in known issue 3. **All 7,770
L356: captures of the table and 990 of the reset rows are attached, each exactly once**, and
L357: every session's attached capture set equals its recorded set exactly. The verifier
L358: checks all of this, plus that no `cmd_id` is claimed twice and that each call's `cmd`
L359: matches the name the robot recorded for that id.
L360: **Truncation.** `command` and `output` are clipped at **2,000 characters, keeping the
L361: head 70% and the tail 30%** with `\n… [N characters omitted] …\n` between them — the
L362: tail is kept because a bridge answer's id and `ok` are at its end. `output_truncated`
L363: flags a clipped **output** (841 steps of the table, 49 of the reset rows); a clipped
L364: *command* has no flag of its own (166 and 19 steps, most of them on steps whose output
L365: was not clipped), so test for the marker if that matters to you. **The model's text is never
L366: truncated**, and the complete, unclipped transcript of every session is always the
L367: file `traces/<session_id>.jsonl`.
